claims.text: 72.25% of adolescent participants (289/400) exhibited some degree of Internet addiction (IAT ≥ 31).
1% of adolescent participants (4/400) exhibited severe Internet addiction.
Internet addiction showed a statistically significant association with age (P < 0.05).
Internet addiction showed a statistically significant association with gender (P < 0.05).
Internet addiction showed a statistically significant association with school type (P < 0.05).
Internet addiction showed a statistically significant association with daily screen time (P < 0.05).
Internet addiction showed a statistically significant association with anxiety severity (P < 0.05).
Multivariable analysis revealed higher odds of Internet addiction among adolescents aged 15–16 years.
Multivariable analysis revealed higher odds of Internet addiction among adolescents attending private schools.
Multivariable analysis revealed higher odds of Internet addiction among adolescents with longer screen time.
Multivariable analysis revealed higher odds of Internet addiction among adolescents with higher levels of anxiety.
Female gender was identified as a risk factor for Internet addiction.
Higher parental education was identified as a risk factor for Internet addiction.
Screen time exceeding 4 hours per day was identified as a risk factor for Internet addiction.

methodologies.name: Cross-sectional survey with IAT and GAD-7
methodologies.description: A school-based cross-sectional study using multistage stratified random sampling, Young’s Internet Addiction Test (IAT), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scale analyzed via Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.
datasets: 400 school-going adolescents aged 12–18 years in Lucknow District, Uttar Pradesh, India
conditions: Multistage stratified random sampling from government and private schools

future_work.text: Comprehensive school-based interventions, including mental health screening and awareness programs, to promote healthy Internet use and psychological wellbeing.
